services.title: Learner records support
services.description: Maintain approved enrollment, progress, and contact records with a visible source trail.
services.intro: Learner details often arrive through forms, email, and staff notes. When updates are copied without a consistent check, incomplete fields and conflicting versions become difficult to resolve.
services.audience: Enrollment coordinators, tutoring programs, cohort operators, and school teams with recurring record updates and a named records owner.
inputs: Approved intake forms or change requests
Field definitions and record status rules
Access to the designated system of record
work: Prepare approved enrollment and contact updates
Check required fields against an agreed checklist
Maintain source links and update notes
Queue corrections and sensitive changes for review
outputs: Exception summary for the records owner
controls: Required field check before completion
Source reference attached to each material change
Access limited to the systems needed for the role
Periodic sample review by the designated records owner
boundaries: The assistant does not decide eligibility, placement, accommodations, discipline, or academic standing.
The organization defines access, retention, consent, and disclosure rules.
Conflicting identity or custody information pauses the workflow for an authorized reviewer.
workflow: Validate the request: Confirm that the request uses an approved source and contains the required identifiers.
Prepare the record: Enter or stage only the permitted fields and preserve the source reference.
Check completeness: Compare the prepared record with the field checklist and flag conflicts rather than resolving them by assumption.
Route the exception: Send sensitive, ambiguous, or policy dependent changes to the accountable records owner.
scenarios: Enrollment packet handoff: Compare an approved packet with the enrollment checklist, prepare complete fields, and return missing documents to the queue.
Contact detail correction: Stage a requested correction with its source and route any conflicting contact or custody detail for review.

faqs.question: Can an assistant approve enrollment?
faqs.answer: No. The assistant can prepare and check records. Eligibility and enrollment approval remain with the authorized team member.

faqs.question: What should we provide first?
faqs.answer: Provide the field checklist, approved source types, system access rules, and the person who reviews exceptions.

faqs.question: How is sensitive information handled?
faqs.answer: Your organization sets access and handling requirements. The role should use least necessary access and a documented escalation path.

services.title: Course administration
services.description: Keep modules, release dates, resources, and routine delivery details aligned to the approved course plan.
services.intro: A course can have sound instruction while its links, dates, module states, and facilitator notes drift apart. Educators then spend delivery time finding preventable setup errors.
services.audience: Course creators, program managers, tutoring organizations, and academic teams running repeatable online or blended courses.
inputs: Current content files and naming rules
work: Build modules from approved course plans
Maintain release calendars and routine settings
Check links, labels, and learner facing files
Track requested changes through review and publication
controls: Prelaunch view using the learner perspective
Version label on approved source files
Two source check for dates that appear in multiple places
Change log with reviewer and publication state
boundaries: Educators retain curriculum, assessment, grading, and instructional decisions.
The assistant does not rewrite substantive content without an approved brief.
Platform changes with unclear learner impact remain unpublished until review.
workflow: Reconcile the plan: Compare the syllabus, course map, and release calendar before making platform changes.
Prepare the build: Create or update modules, links, labels, and settings from approved material.
Run the delivery check: Inspect learner visibility, links, dates, and file versions against the launch checklist.
Publish or route: Publish only where authority is documented and route instructional uncertainty to the content owner.
scenarios: New cohort setup: Duplicate an approved course shell, replace cohort dates, verify visibility, and present the shell for owner review.
Content revision release: Replace the approved file, check every linked location, record the version, and archive the superseded asset.

faqs.question: Can the assistant design the curriculum?
faqs.answer: Not within this service. The assistant administers approved material while the educator owns curriculum and teaching choices.

faqs.question: Which platform can this support?
faqs.answer: The workflow can be adapted to your learning platform when access, conventions, and a review path are available.

faqs.question: Should the assistant publish changes directly?
faqs.answer: Only when publication authority and a tested checklist are explicit. New or high impact changes should be reviewed first.

services.title: Education scheduling support
services.description: Coordinate sessions, availability, approved reminders, and calendar exceptions without making program decisions.
services.intro: Scheduling becomes expensive when availability, room or meeting links, attendance expectations, and exceptions live in separate conversations.
services.audience: Tutors, cohort programs, faculty support teams, and learning organizations with repeated sessions across people and time zones.
work: Collect availability through an approved process
Prepare and update session calendars
Send approved confirmations and reminders
Identify conflicts, missing details, and unresolved exceptions
controls: Time zone shown in confirmations
Meeting link and access check before the session
Calendar and source request reconciled after changes
Unconfirmed sessions remain visibly open
boundaries: The assistant does not decide attendance consequences, staffing priorities, or accommodation requests.
Educators decide whether missed instruction changes a learner plan.
Urgent welfare or safeguarding messages bypass routine scheduling and go to the named response path.
workflow: Gather constraints: Collect availability, duration, location, access, and deadline details in one scheduling record.
Prepare the option: Apply documented rules to produce a proposed time or an exception list.
Confirm the schedule: Send the approved confirmation and update the shared calendar and session record.
Monitor changes: Process routine changes and route conflicts that require a policy or priority decision.
scenarios: Weekly tutoring rota: Collect tutor availability, apply the approved matching rules, and route unmatched learners to the program lead.
Virtual class readiness: Verify calendar entry, host, link, participant message, and materials before the scheduled session.

faqs.question: Can the assistant choose which learner gets priority?
faqs.answer: No. Priority rules must come from the program owner. Uncovered cases are escalated.

faqs.question: Can reminders be automated?
faqs.answer: Routine approved reminders can use platform automation after the timing, audience, and exception path are tested.

faqs.question: What happens when a teacher cancels?
faqs.answer: The assistant follows the approved cancellation path, records affected sessions, and routes decisions about substitutes or makeups.

services.title: Family and learner communication
services.description: Prepare and route routine approved messages while preserving human judgment for sensitive conversations.
services.intro: Routine questions can crowd out complex learner support, yet a fast response is not useful if it lacks context, promises an outcome, or misses a sensitive concern.
services.audience: Schools, tutoring programs, course teams, and learner support operations with recurring questions and status messages.
inputs: Current program facts and contact directory
work: Triage inbound messages by approved categories
Draft or send routine template based replies
Record contact attempts and stated next steps
Route instructional, welfare, complaint, and policy questions
controls: Source check for dates, policies, and status
Recipient and attachment check before sending
Clear next owner on every escalated item
Routine review of templates and repeated unanswered questions
boundaries: The assistant does not give instructional, clinical, legal, disciplinary, or safeguarding advice.
Complaints and emotionally sensitive messages move to the accountable team member.
A template is never used to imply a decision that has not been made.
workflow: Read for intent and risk: Identify the request, required context, and any trigger that needs immediate human attention.
Verify the facts: Check the approved source before preparing a routine response.
Respond or route: Use the approved language for in scope questions and transfer judgment based messages with context.
Record the handoff: Log the response, status, next owner, and promised follow up without adding unsupported conclusions.
scenarios: Program logistics question: Confirm the published session detail, answer with the approved template, and record the interaction.
Learner support concern: Acknowledge receipt without interpreting the concern, preserve the relevant context, and route it to the designated support owner.

faqs.question: Can the assistant answer academic questions?
faqs.answer: The assistant can route them and share approved logistical information. Teaching and academic judgment stay with educators.

faqs.question: Can the role manage a shared inbox?
faqs.answer: Yes, when categories, templates, access, response targets, and urgent escalation triggers are documented.

faqs.question: How do we avoid impersonal replies?
faqs.answer: Use templates as controlled source language, then allow relevant factual context within a clear tone guide and review process.

services.title: Resource library support
services.description: Organize approved learning materials so teams can identify the current, accessible, and intended version.
services.intro: A folder can contain useful material and still be hard to use. Ambiguous names, duplicates, missing accessibility status, and outdated links make staff recheck the same resources.
services.audience: Course teams, tutoring organizations, training programs, and educators maintaining shared banks of learning material.
work: Inventory and classify approved resources
Apply naming, folder, and metadata conventions
Track review and version status
Route accessibility, rights, or content questions to owners
outputs: Broken link and unresolved issue queue
controls: Stable naming and required metadata fields
Link and permission test from the intended user view
Visible owner and review date
Archive record for superseded material
boundaries: Educators decide instructional suitability and sequence.
Qualified owners determine accessibility conformance and usage rights.
The assistant does not delete or replace source material without an approved archive rule.
workflow: Inventory the collection: List each resource, location, format, stated audience, owner, and current status.
Normalize the metadata: Apply approved names, categories, version labels, and review dates without changing instructional meaning.
Check usability: Test access and links, note accessibility status, and identify duplicate or orphaned material.
Publish the index: Make the approved collection findable and send unresolved content, rights, or access questions to their owners.
scenarios: Tutor resource bank: Index approved worksheets by level and topic, identify duplicates, and expose the current version to tutors.
Accessible material request: Record the requested format, locate the approved source file, and route conversion and approval to the responsible owner.

faqs.question: Can the assistant choose the best teaching resource?
faqs.answer: No. The role can improve discovery and status. An educator decides instructional suitability.

faqs.question: Will this fix inaccessible files?
faqs.answer: The assistant can identify and track status. Remediation and conformance decisions stay with people assigned that responsibility.

faqs.question: Where should the library live?
faqs.answer: Use the approved platform that your intended users can access. The operating model matters more than a particular tool.

services.title: Reporting preparation
services.description: Compile traceable operational summaries so education leaders can review evidence and make decisions.
services.intro: Leaders lose review time when each update uses different definitions, missing periods, or figures detached from their source. Preparation needs consistency without turning an assistant into the analyst or decision maker.
services.audience: Program leads, school operations teams, tutoring managers, and course businesses with recurring status and activity reviews.
work: Collect approved data from named sources
Reconcile required periods and definitions
Prepare tables, status views, and exception notes
Package source references for accountable review
outputs: Open question list for the report owner
controls: Period and definition check before compilation
Source reference for each reported measure
Reconciliation totals where the data permits
Reviewer signoff before external distribution
boundaries: The assistant does not certify accuracy, interpret causation, or make strategic decisions.
Metric definitions and materiality thresholds come from the report owner.
Sensitive exports follow the organization’s access, storage, and deletion requirements.
workflow: Confirm the brief: Verify the period, definitions, audience, format, and cut off time before collecting data.
Compile the source set: Gather approved exports or records and note their retrieval time and scope.
Run preparation checks: Reconcile totals, missing fields, duplicates, and period coverage using the supplied rules.
Package for review: Present the summary with caveats, source references, and open exceptions for the accountable analyst or leader.
scenarios: Cohort operations summary: Compile approved enrollment and session status counts, flag missing records, and provide the source list to the program lead.
Access review preparation: Organize the current access export by approved role definitions and route unexpected permissions to the system owner.

faqs.question: Does the assistant analyze performance?
faqs.answer: The assistant can prepare consistent views and flag exceptions. Interpretation and decisions remain with the accountable leader or analyst.

faqs.question: Can reports be sent to families or funders?
faqs.answer: Only after an authorized owner reviews the content, audience, disclosure basis, and distribution method.

faqs.question: What makes a report review-ready?
faqs.answer: It uses agreed definitions and periods, identifies sources and gaps, and makes unresolved questions visible.

services.title: Admissions inquiry support
services.description: Give routine program inquiries a clear record, approved response, and accountable next step.
services.intro: Give routine program inquiries a clear record, approved response, and accountable next step. A focused administrative role maintains the agreed record and prepares useful next actions, with exceptions kept visible for the person who has authority to resolve them.
services.audience: school leaders, course creators, tutors, and education teams
inputs: The current workflow, source systems, and approved access
Your templates, definitions, and completion criteria
A named review owner, communication cadence, and escalation rules
work: Log program inquiries in the approved system
Share current published program information and application steps
Track missing administrative documents against your checklist
Route eligibility, placement, and sensitive questions to the admissions owner
controls: Compare each completed item with its approved source.
Check that the status, owner, and next action agree across records.
Keep missing or conflicting information visible until the review owner resolves it.
Review a sample together before expanding the volume or scope.
boundaries: No admissions, eligibility, placement, financial-aid, or accommodation decisions
Only approved information is shared under your organization’s access rules
Requests involving student safety, protected records, or staff performance go to the designated school leader without an independent determination.
workflow: Agree on the first queue, the expected output, and who reviews the work.
Walk through representative records together and document ambiguous cases.
Begin with a manageable volume and a regular exception review.
Use corrections and completion checks to refine the handoff before expanding it.
scenarios: A recurring admissions inquiry support queue needs consistent attention while your manager focuses on decisions.
Several people contribute information, and the reviewer needs one current record with visible gaps.

faqs.question: What should we prepare for this role?
faqs.answer: Bring a current example, the approved source systems, the output you need, and the manager who can answer questions. Together we define what complete means and which situations must be escalated.

faqs.question: Can we begin with a limited scope?
faqs.answer: Yes. Start with one repeatable queue, review a sample of completed work, and improve the instructions before adding responsibilities.

faqs.question: Who handles exceptions or consequential decisions?
faqs.answer: Your authorized owner does. Support collects the context and records the question so the decision can be made by the right person, then follows the approved instruction.
